data.title: Building Systems Reachable From the Corporate Network
data.summary: Access control, CCTV, intercom and building management systems were reachable from the corporate network, ran unsupported software, and in places retained default credentials — so the physical controls could be defeated from a keyboard.
data.description:
Building systems are computers that nobody treats as computers. They are installed by a contractor, commissioned once, and left: unpatched, unmonitored, and frequently still carrying the vendor's default credentials.

Their function is what makes this serious. Control of the access system means unlocking doors, enrolling a credential, and editing the log that records it. Control of CCTV means viewing, and deleting, the footage of the entry. Control of building management means doors held open on a fire signal, and environmental control of a server room.

They are typically reachable from the ordinary corporate network, and often from the internet through a vendor's remote support arrangement that nobody reviews.
data.recommendation:
* Place building systems on a dedicated segment with no route from user networks and no inbound internet access.
* Change default credentials and apply firmware updates, as a contractual requirement on the installer.
* Review vendor remote access: named accounts, MFA, and access only during an agreed window.
* Export access and camera logs to a system the building controller cannot alter.
data.short_recommendation: Segment building systems and change their default credentials.
